notes.title: Hokko Life l World Shrines Update!
notes.content:
Hey there, Pals! 

We hope you're ready for the next update! This includes a HUGE host of fixes, changes, improvements and additions to Hokko Life! Read all about it below 👀 

More Space! 🏘️
We're super excited to announce that you will now be able to EXPAND your housing! Interact with a home to add either a roomy upstairs or downstairs, yours to decorate however you please! 

https://i.imgur.com/yWAnLlH.gif

World Shrines 🔮
Travelling has never been easier, with World Shrines! Donate resources to shrines to unlock them, and teleport between locations! 

https://i.imgur.com/9N18JmH.gif

My Designs Tab 🎨 
You will now be able to see and manage your created and downloaded designs! In the My Designs Tab you can delete creations, as well as see how much space each one takes up. 

https://i.imgur.com/T3Ucnoi.gif

The Barn! 👩‍🌾
We've added a new location! You can now go inside, and decorate the small barn on Aubrey's Farm! 

https://i.imgur.com/1krZzZL.gif

Bug Fixes & Improvements! 🛠️
In addition to all the above, we've also worked hard to include a HUGE amount of various fixes, changes and improvements in this update! 

In particular, the Mayor Merits screen has been reworked, and now gives hints on how to use unlocked features! Some merits have also had their requirements lowered, to make them easier to unlock. Thanks to the feedback we received from players, we have also improved the main intro flow to guide new players through the beginning of the game, as well as added an on-screen guide so you’ll always know what needs doing next! 

Thank you to our fantastic community for your continuous feedback and support! Find the full list of patch notes for this update below.

Patch Notes

New Additions!

 Community: Expandable Housing: Interact with a home to add either an upstairs or downstairs room!
 World Shrines: Donate resources to shrines around the world to unlock them and teleport between locations!
 Added a quest tracker on the HUD, showing main quest steps, as well as any villager requests the player is tracking
 Community: Added a tab for Player Creations in the Design Tool, from here you can:
 Browse all the furniture creations in the game’s save data and:
 Craft a copy of any of the designs
 See how much disk space each design takes up
 Delete designs
 See how much space all of your furniture creations take up relative to how much space is available
 New Barn location! You can now go inside the small barn on Aubrey’s Farm


Changes

 Removed edge blur from dialogue ui
 Creator code is now saved after first online connection, speeding up saving of creations and fixing an issue that could be caused if there was no internet connection when saving.
 Community: Bridge and stairs placement is less strict about rotations
 Community: Intro quests now count towards “requests completed” stat
 Weed respawn rates are no longer tied to real-world days
 Worked into the Mayor Merit screen to make gameplay merits more visible as well as what stats are required easier to read.

 Community: Broken chair leg request is now unlocked after the player has completed the pickaxe quest
 Deconstruct option on the Crafting Bench is now blocked until after initial crafting tutorial
 Community: Added location, bait and name information for fish/bugs on tournament leaderboards
 Community: Lowered amount of designs required before the Bomb Merit unlocks
 Community: Lowered sprinting requirement for some Mayor Merits
 Lights in homes are on by default the first time you enter them
 Villagers with requests are more likely to appear when populating a location with random villagers so that players can spend less time having to hunt villagers.
 Community: Lowered time requirement on design requests
 Added legal text to main menu
 Community: Boosts to fish probability when in a fishing tournament
 Blue flower is now more blue
 Optimised weed meshes


Fixes

 Fix for issue where placing of an object like the bridge is blocked because its bobbing animation goes too high 
 Fixed texture on house windows
 Cursor now follows scrollbar when using controller to scroll, preventing cursor going to strange places

 Community: Fix for starting villagers not being correctly set up, resulting in dialogue missing and softlock when trying to talk to them.
 Fix for issue that could cause starting villagers’ home levels not to load
 Community: Fixed issue where multi-produce requests for Oma aka recipe requests, weren’t replacing previous requests

notes.title: Hokko Life l Full Launch & Desert Island Distractions Update OUT NOW!
notes.content:
Hey there folks! 

We're so, so excited to announce... 

We have launched out of Steam Early Access! 🥳💗 

Thank you for all your support during our Early Access journey. We really do appreciate all of your feedback, and continue to do so as we continue to work on Hokko Life.

We have also dropped the latest update! 

Just a side note - if you have not played Hokko Life in a while, we'd recommend starting a new save file as many updates have happened during our Early Access journey which could affect the file itself. 

Please find all the highlights and the full patch notes below for the latest update! 👇

Desert Island Distractions

https://i.imgur.com/GvVg0n5.gif

New Content! 🏖️
We're so excited to bring you lots of new content with this update! Speak to Hurley in the Inn, and hop on his boat to a new location! Discover a tropical island brimming with new life, and secrets... 

https://i.imgur.com/5anolqB.gif

New Species and Materials! 🦋
Discover and add new species of tropical butterflies, ocean and pond fish to your collection! Not only that, we've added new design tool materials! You can now use bamboo, driftwood and shells to create whatever you desire 🎋

https://i.imgur.com/MTX7xpD.gif

Archaeology 🏺
Master the Artefact detector, and help Leonard find hidden artefacts all around the island! Pop into the mines and use this to discover geodes containing rare gems you'll be able to use to enhance your designs! 💎✨ 

To break geodes, simply go to the crafting bench and select "break geode". You won't know what gem is hidden in there until you do! 👀

https://i.imgur.com/aSlhi1Q.gif

Meet A New Friend! 🐱
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/65123b3e68530157f29c8b6cad562c703caa1f62.png

Our newest villager Ramesh, designed by community member Nisrii, is looking for a new place to live! Be sure to welcome them with open arms! 

Steamdeck Support and Steam Achievements ⚙️
You asked, we delivered! Hokko Life is now supported on Steamdeck! You're also now able to unlock Steam Achievements! 

Key Bug Fixes & Changes 🐛 
Thank you for all your feedback as we work towards the Early Access release date. This update will have LOTS of bug fixes, including those raised by you, the community! Find just a few of the key fixes below:  


 Fix for several backpack issues, including items getting added to a slot in the backpack outside its capacity, causing it to not appear in the UI.  
 Fixes for produce requests! 
 Several fixes for floating objects after placing them. 
 Fixes for 16:10 aspect ratio! 

… and lots, lots more! We really do appreciate all your bug reports, as we continue to work on Hokko Life! Please be reminded, just because we're launching out of Early Access, this doesn't mean we're done just yet - we're working on more stuff for future updates which we'll share as soon as we can! 💕

If you haven't already, check out the August Devlog that mentions some of what's potentially to come (including teleportation shrines, and house expansions)! 

We’ve included the full patch notes for this update below, so keep reading for all the details for this update! 👇 

Patch Notes

notes.title: A pretty hefty devlog!
notes.content:
Well well well! It's been a little while hasn't it!?

A lot has happened since the last post in May! Hokko Life got released into Early Access! Crazy stuff!

I thought I'd spend this devlog just giving my thoughts on how things have been going since then, how the launch was, and some info on things moving forward.

Launch
To be honest, the launch ended up being pretty chill, haha! I had prepared the launch build a few days in advance, and so when it came to launch time there were thankfully no last-minute surprises or frantic bug fixing going on. As Team17 handles releases there's a nice process in place where each build we make live has to be verified and approved by their test department. Without this it would be very tempting to work on the build up until the very last second, which given the size of the game could mean the introduction of new bugs, and that's the last thing we want! 

I think having the beta not too long before Early Access meant that the impact of the release was far less stressful; I'd gained some experience from doing a launch, and seeing players enjoy the game and report bugs etc for the beta meant that when it came to the "real thing" I was thankfully not overwhelmed! At the same time, I've been through a fair few game launches now to know that they're actually not as crazy or scary as one imagines!

For the actual launch itself, Team17 handled the process so all I could do was sit back and wait for the game to go on sale; which was definitely a very weird feeling. Being so disconnected to a big event for something you've been building by yourself for 4 or so years, no buttons for me to press, was a tad surreal! I spent my time eating some lovely Vietnamese food and watching streamers play the game, while hanging out in Discord chatting to everyone. It was definitely a very cozy launch!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/3034ef7092cd41904c1027c63c2e730eb558d2c3.png

RawX put on a lovely little show to celebrate the launch of the game!

Post Launch & July
I'm sure you've noticed, but the rest of June and July was a little bit frantic! I did a lot of bug fixing, trying to solve some of the biggest issues quickly so that more and more players could enjoy the game; for a period of time we were putting out weekly patches, which is very tiring, especially as a solo developer! 

Alongside the patches I was working on the Farming update too. Farming was one of the areas that had been started a long time ago, but sadly could not be finished in time for the June release date; but this meant that thankfully the ground work was already there. That's not to say there wasn't a lot of work and bug-fixing involved, but luckily it wasn't as much work as building new features from scratch!

Moving forward
So now the initial launch and first-update craziness is out of the way, how are things looking? Well, I've been working with Team17 to finalise the roadmap over the Early Access period; setting dates to each update and generally getting a plan in place for how I'll be working for the whole duration. Getting this plan in place also means that marketing, sales etc all know when big events will be hitting and can plan their activities accordingly. 

With the dust settled a bit, I've been spending this month getting around to fixing some of the larger, more complicated bugs that have been hanging over me and stopping some players from enjoying the game. It feels great to have been able to get those fixed and I'm looking forward to getting the next patch out so that I can finally put those bugs behind me!

Like I mentioned, releasing a patch every week is very tiring, and it really isn't something that's sustainable. After the initial burst of fire-fighting patches the goal moving forward is to release larger, less frequent updates; alternating between Quality of Life & bug-fix updates and bigger feature updates. This means I can sustain a good pace without destroying myself; we get more time for updates to be properly tested before being released; and there's a reliable pace that players can expect, rather than everything being a bit uncertain and muddled.

With things calmer now, and having shipped the first big farming update, it makes good sense for me to take a little bit of vacation and recouperate. It's been a very exhausting year or so up to release and there have been a lot of difficult hurdles, stressful weeks and frantic workdays. I can feel I'm definitely in need of some rest and relaxation; I'm pretty tired, and I could do with a recharge! I'll be taking two weeks now, and my plan is to do as little as possible; hopefully if the weather stays good I can spend some time at my allotment, gardening and generally enjoying the fresh air!

Reception
I wanted to finish this devlog by thanking everyone who's supported the game! I'm always blown away by the kindness and encouragement of the community and it makes me so happy to see everyone sharing their creations, as well as suporting and helping one another. 

On the subject of creations, I have no befind-the-scenes development images to share this month, so I wanted to share some shots of some of the amazing objects that have caught my eye over the last few weeks!

I hope you're all keeping well, take care of yourselves and I'll speak to you soon!

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #10
notes.content:
Devlog: January 2021

Well well, January disappeared fast didn't it!? In a blur of dark winter days and a little snow work continued on Hokko. So let's have a peek at what got done!

Lighting
I fixed up the lighting setup in the game so that it does things properly as opposed to the sort of half-finished setup I had before. This has meant the world and items have started to sit a lot better together, and have a more uniform look. Alongside this I went in and configured lighting for the different times of day, as well as several different summer weather types: sunshine, overcast and rainy. 

To help me configure the lighting I built an editor window that allows me to change between times of day and weather when the game is running, and then live-edit colours for things like the sky, and tweak values for the sun intensity and other stuff. It made previewing and working on the lighting a lot more pleasant!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/3e908535a2d43edcd3fe200cc51c1c3d527991c6.jpg
The Lighting Editor

I also made sure things like the lights on streetlamps and houses were working too, and I managed to find an ambient occlusion setup that supports my custom-lit character shaders! (Ambient Occlusion is an effect that gives the appearance of contact shadows and darkens areas in crevices etc, where light naturally doesn't reach)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/4608d7729b6751ad48a3d02e542528da20a543e3.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/758963079a083d79a91fb7b0d72372d9615bc40e.jpg
Timeline of Lighting on Sunny and Overcast Days

Game Intro
Most of my time this month was spent between two things, the game intro, and usability testing preparations. I completely reworked the start of the game, adding a small cutscene as well as going through and setting up quests for the player that guide them into the game.

By completing small requests for the villagers, you'll learn and unlock the systems in the game, and my work this month was focussed on writing the dialogue for these, as well as locking off parts of the game until the player reached certain parts of the quest line.

I even set up a very short cutscene that hints at your arrival in the world. It's really not much, but is far better than nothing!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/e77fe1d3cc10c86ffe0584c0cb44ce6db4d2818c.jpg
Shot from intro cutscene

Usability Test
Like I say, the other major time-sync of this month was getting things ready for usability testing. What this means is we set a bunch of testers on the game to gain feedback on areas that are confusing, or that they struggle with. Doing this enables us to get really useful info on what parts of the game could do with some work on user experience. It's very easy to not see these issues when you're working on the game, as you understand how everything works; so getting fresh player eyes on it is extremely valuable. To make sure the build of the game the testers were playing was stable and had most of the rough edges smoothed out I spent a bunch of time this month squishing bugs and making tweaks. 

I've not got the results back yet, but I know it's going to be very interesting to see what their report says!

Mine
With some of the remaining time I spent a day or two on the mine/cave part of the world. I replaced the old wall graphics with new meshes and also implemented a gameplay idea I'd had for a while.... darkness!

You won't be able to stray too far away from the light in the caves now, and will need to place out light sources to enable you to see and head deeper into the mines. This really enhances the feeling of exploration as you move further and further into the darkness and I think it offers a nice change of pace and gameplay feel to the rest of the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/85b62412aa8f4645fd5a33d550a040d7bf03b322.jpg
Placing lanterns in the mine to progress

Bomb
The bomb got a little bit of love too this month, updating the graphics with those done by another artist, and also setting up a proper throw animation. I added a fuse and flashing effect too. I'll be adding the explosion fx a little later, right now i'm using a very placeholder sphere!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/32b455f98b5035f161ed9e4e98686dbef6f18c16.gif
New bomb graphics, throw animation, fuse, and flashing effect

More Art
The artists over at Team 17 have been beavering away producing more and more art for the game. Including:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/55ff441e0245552138db9b9e1f2d74c0d0225f02.jpg
New Houses!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/faa326767c5487f208e4f91d01e7f11113bf3a43.jpg
Flowers!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/e52d153bf0cdb75811f9ad58f0efff96839a81dc.jpg
Updated graphics for the general store!

They also got started on the new character meshes, which I'm very much looking forward to sharing with you in the coming updates!

So there have it! Already we're part of the way into 2021, and more and more areas of the game are getting a lot of visual love. It's really coming along well!

I hope you're all keeping well, thankyou as always for your continued support!

Let me know your thoughts in the comments, and I'll speak to you all again soon!

from Robert

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #9
notes.content:
Devlog: December 2020

Well, it's certainly a bit weird writing December's update in January, after two weeks "out of office"... Trying to remember what got done is a little tricky, but let's have a look-see...

Updated Collection Book

The Collection Book is an interface in the game that lists all of the things you've caught in the game; including fish and insects. It's your primary record of what you've caught, what you've got left to catch, and your size records for each creature. The old UI was a bit limited, ugly, and very clunky; so it got replaced this month!

The new Interface is built with "The Future in Mind" (TM) so the layout is flexible and will easily allow us to add more creatures over time to the world, without having to spend time updating the Collection Book Interface. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/aea343f81b6f0199550c06168877b992dad1c6d4.png
Updated Collection Book

Alongside this there was a minor rework in how fish and insects are classified, and thus how they spawn in the world. Creatures are now separated into more distinct groups, and this makes it easier for the player to know where certain insects or fish can be caught, for example; and it also means we can more elegantly categorise them in the Collection Book. We've also been talking about attaching achievements to different categories too (for example catching 5 river fish)

Insect Behaviour

I went in and updated how the insects behave in the world; pretty much ripping out the old system and replacing it. Butterflies now have a stamina, and will fly for a while before needing to rest. I added the ability to add "land points" on objects, so that butterflies will land on one of these locations if there's one nearby. Locations can be rocks, bushes, flowers, trees and so on.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/cf9a90973b9f3eab42fee5ae33ebea7beed86683.gif
Butterfly resting on a rock

Art created a new butterfly mesh and textures this month and I added a simple skeleton to the mesh in order to give butterflies a more fluid set of animations.

Fishing Rework

I've been bothered by the fishing mini game in Hokko for a little while. Although it's fun and provides a nice challenge, I felt that it was very confusing and really hard to integrate visually into the rest of the experience. I'd been mulling over a big change to the mini game over the previous months, and decided to implement it in December. The old mini game was replaced with something that's less intrusive, less punishing, and hopefully a lot easier to understand. The mini game also allows us to expand the game with upgradable rods if we want to later on.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/6539c8816b382e1985980c9e26305ce685a5a570.png
Updated fishing minigame

Alongside an updated minigame, I worked into the fish's behaviour. I changed how they spawn in the world to use a mesh instead of just spawning around a set point; this means we can set up a simple mesh that defines an area fish should be and they'll spawn and keep within that mesh. I also reworked how they detect bait to make their behaviour more understandable, and also... less stupid (often they'd just swim past bait in front of them and you needed to be pretty accurate with where you cast your line, which wasn't very enjoyable!)

Adding other items to your creations

I made a minor tweak to the Design Tool to give players the ability to add other types of items to their creations. These objects can be flagged in Unity as items that can be used, and they'll show up in the new backpack section of the design tool. Right now this includes fish and insects, but we can flag any item we want players to be able to use in their designs.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/a44bff200f9e4cdfb77256a38c2ff817a8d21a7d.png
Using Fish in a design

On top of this I worked into the villager requests to give them the ability to request designs using a specific item or theme. Villagers can now request a wooden chair, or a chair using butterflies in the design, for example. While I was in the code I also made their behaviour with design requests a bit more forgiving. If you don't spend very long on a design, or it's very basic, or you've not done what they've asked, they'll let you know and give you the item back for re-work; before they'd just be a bit miffed and take the item from you anyway, which meant it was hard to know what you'd done to upset them!

Tying stuff to real-world time

I quite like the feeling in games where there are changes that happen over real-world time; giving the player the excitement of coming back to the game every day to see what's new or changed. This can be things like what items are available in a store, what characters are in-town, that kind of thing. In Hokko this stuff was tied to game-time, which removed that "play a little a day" feeling you get from other titles. Although I don't want to tie the entirety of Hokko to real-world time, as I feel this limits the enjoyment you can get from the title (if you work during the daytime, the only part of a real-time game you can experience is the evening, which I think is unfair) I decided to make some parts of the experience connected to the real-world clock. These include what items are in stores, what characters will come visit your town, and how quickly things like weeds and dig-spots pop up. I think this change will give Hokko a good balance from both worlds.

Save game tweaks

I made some small but important changes to the save game system; I made the save games a bit less easy to cheat in, and I also set them up to store the game version too. Storing the game version in all files that I save means that we can better handle future updates that may have big changes that require converting save games and thus hopefully saves me a lot of pain in the future!

Main Menu

The Main Menu scene was updated this month with all the new art assets, the animations that Alex has provided, and the music from Chris. It was really wonderful being able to tie it all together; taking the idea I had originally and then using the parts created to build it and realise that vision!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/24eb98c4ac4134e556f41644d37b2fe8fe588725.png
Updated main menu

Emotes Chooser

Alex had done a bunch of emote animations for me over the previous months; these will be used in conversation, but also can now be triggered by the player. I added a simple menu that allows you to choose an emote to play; giving players an additional way of expressing themselves in the game! I'm looking forward to working into the conversation system when we have the new villagers in the game and giving them the emotes during conversations too.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/457b96bafcc9b8c44d3bd2c502db052716ee47cf.png
Emote UI

Home start Layouts

Starting villagers now have stuff in their homes! Up until now they'd have an empty home, which wasn't exactly fair, so I made it so that starting characters will have fill their homes with stuff. We can define layouts for different types of villagers and then the system will use one of these layouts when the game sets up the town for the first time. Even though at the moment there's only one layout (art will be adding more later on) just having a home with stuff in, already in the town when you move in makes the world feel a lot more alive!

More Stuff!

The Artists got some more stuff into the game, including bits of furniture and instruments!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/05badd0dbd187d2e4a01cf500e2237fee10018f7.png
More Stuff!

Holiday Work

During the last week of my time off I spent a little time playing the game and doing some minor tweaks. Mostly small things that popped up during gameplay, and some other "non-essential" things I've wanted to get into the project for a while:

 I reworked the animation setup (again) for the avatar, and made things more immediate and hopefully less prone to error.
 I changed how rotation works in the Design Tool to make it less clunky and more useable on a gamepad. It felt horrible before but now feels pretty nice!
 I tweaked the speech bubble appearance, and worked into some areas of the UI to make them animate better and be more rewarding.
 All interfaces that allow you to pick a number (selling, crafting, etc) now let the player press left to "loop" the amount back around to the maximum amount; making selling all of an item, or crafting the maximum amount super easy!
 Set up the project using Assembly Definition files to break it into sections making compilation of changes quicker
 Separated logging into a custom function to allow easy control for turning it on/off
 Changed the function used for random numbers to one that's EVEN MORE RANDOM!


And there we have it. Turns out quite a bit got done in December, even though it was a short month!

I hope you've all had a relaxing festive period; I came back to the project full of energy and excitement and I'm really looking forward to 2021 and the year of Hokko!

Thanks for your support, and as always, let me know your thoughts in the comments!

from Robert

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #8
notes.content:
Devlog: November 2020

Well, 2020 is fast reaching its end (thank the stars!) and the days are getting shorter and colder. The changes to Hokko this month were few, but all of them quite a bit of work. Let's take a look and see!

Map Generation

I was running around the world of Hokko recently and thinking about how it felt. I realised the area that you naturally gravitate towards for customisation felt impersonal and didn't really invite creativity. It was cramped and had a set layout, which would mean all player's towns would be somewhat similar as they started from the same base. 

I decided to tackle this in November, and set about setting up a simple map generator for this area. As it's so late in development I didn't have the time to do anything really complex, so I came up with a simple system that combines level "pieces" together in random combinations to give around 60 different variations. This system can be expanded on later on too, with more pieces added to give even more variety. At the same time I more than doubled the space available, so there's more space for homes and decoration.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/9a995fb93ed8aa61b8c57bd31c4606b05ecc3baf.png

One of the large pieces used in level generation

The new layouts generated feel a lot more unique and interesting, and provide plenty of areas for players to get creative with. I'm really happy I made the decision to do this, as it really alters how the game feels and your relation to it!

Level Updates

Alongside the rework of the "home area" I also tackled two other levels in the world which I felt lacked any good direction. They felt a bit strange and uninteresting, so I spent a day or so on each and changed their layouts.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/c8c46788f4732cc322f0ab588d8df54ed3438961.png
The grove area got expanded, opened up and its pond enlarged

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/eb56417c988623d020185e85e1706d2b2bfe4317.png
The small wood area also got opened up, given a better layout and features a different type of tree

Online

After some discussions I decided to partner with LootLocker for the backend services for Hokko Life and set about implementing it into the project this month. They provide a service for uploading/downloading player content, as well as a whole host of other things, and have been working with me to build out LootLocker to fit Hokko Life. 

It took a little while getting the fundamentals running, but now the game works well and players are again able to upload and download furniture. I used this time too to add the "weekly challenges" to the game. Each week there will be a theme set up, and we'll pick out our favourite creations from the community that match this theme to showcase on the start screen of the catalogue. Players can then download these creations into their game to decorate their world, or even add their own twist to them in the Design Tool.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/d9044379f72afe78d4cf35eb3dacbbfaba32cb07.png
You'll use a computer in the world to access the catalogue, and so the ui is styled a bit like an old computer

Icons

Jonas continued this month working on icons and patterns for various parts of the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/838d11d180e26ac6744750dfc74e917b1bf3e4c1.png
Icons

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/38eb37497d3c59eb9385af2589bfe9711ab08cd0.png
Patterns

Animations

Alex has also been continuing with animation work this month, and has produced a bunch of lovely new animations for the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/5be21b0f5daaf66875fd6fc1817684a949a31dfd.gif
Thinking

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/f5555341e2397514ac8b923bd0b6042488d0f80a.gif
Digging

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/da142d9a5366758da8b966cb797ab10954b093e2.gif
Changing your outfit

Art

The artists over at Team 17 have been continuing to add items to the game, so there's more and more stuff you can decorate houses with!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/6f19aa1be8da074099f5f477e93940610ceda7d0.png
New items

They also got started on reworking the fish in the game!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/a7a36bf25f95b5336aa34225d76d99da5da4ff84.png
Look how cute this little one is!


So there we have it. Now we're headed into December, and a very different Christmas this year. I'll be taking a little time to myself in December, but as I can't visit my family, I'll be spending some more time with Hokko before 2021, trying to get a head-start on next year!

I hope you're all keeping well, and I'll speak to you soon!

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #7
notes.content:
Here’s an update from Robert at Wonderscope Games on what he got up to on Hokko Life last month!


Bye bye October 👋

We got a lot done during you, and you gave us some wonderful Autumn weather! 

UI Improvements
Continuing from last month I worked on updating more of the UI in the game to the new style, as well as fixing lots of niggling bugs and improving general interactions.

The catch/collect short cutscene got some polish, cleaning up the ui and adding things like blur.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/21e2ad873a750ca5456473080bf99af81a22eb79.png


The carpenter store got a lick of paint too. This is where you'll go to unlock new crafting recipes, creation blueprints, paintbrushes etc.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/7f08b118b27ce852232ef8e5d0b04e14356a09af.png

I added interact prompts when you get close to an interactable object, telling you what interactions you can perform.

https://i.imgur.com/OJuV9K9.gif

I updated the placement mode, moving the camera up and giving you a better view when decorating. I also added interact hints to tell you how to control the mode.


https://i.imgur.com/AaNPg77.gif

Sprinting
A while back I added jumping to the game as a new mechanic for getting around. It coincided with me trying out an stamina/energy system. After playing with jump and the energy stuff in the game, I realised it really didn't fit Hokko, and so removed it. 

I decided to add a sprint to the game, this helps you get around a lot quicker, and also gives the player something to do while they're running across levels (I found I was jumping while running around to fill the time, and sprint makes a lot more sense)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/826c289fc5cd6cb3a111bdbff79b065eea8de3e4.png

You'll now have an energy meter just for sprinting, which will deplete as you sprint and waiting a little while will refill it.

It was a small change, but makes a huge difference to how it feels to get around!

Dialogue System Update
I replaced my system for animating text in dialogue with a better one from the Unity Asset Store (one that I've had my eye on for a while and was on sale recently, hehe)

I hooked this up, and re-jigged my dialogue system to allow for emotes and text highlighting to happen at points in the dialogue text; which wasn't possible with the old system.

With this new system I can add things like camera shake to dialogue too! 

https://i.imgur.com/2ZQuWJ7.gif
New dialogue text and camera shake

Requests
I built upon the request system in the game this month, adding some new requests as well as improving those already there.

The villagers ask you for things every now and then, sometimes they'll ask you to design furniture, and sometimes they'll ask for a specific item, or to deliver something. On top of this I added requests for tidying up the town (removing weeds etc) and requests to decorate either the interior or exterior of a villger's home. 

I also extended the design furniture request and added a stage where the player needs to place the item in the villager's home before their task is "done". This was done in combination with adding a rating system to the request, which will look at how much effort was spent on an item and adjust the reward accordingly. If you do a bad job of a piece of furniture, you'll now get a disappointed response, a low reward, and the villager might just throw your creation away!

I had been discussing progression with my design help over at Team 17, and we decided to move some unlocks onto the villagers themselves. I improved on the reward part of requests to allow for a chance that you'll get a "special reward". These special rewards are rare, and they unlock items in either the Farming or Carpenter stores. This way, by helping villagers out, you'll unlock more of the game over time too!

Town Rating
I had also discussed the idea of a "town rating" with Team 17, which would act as a behind-the-scenes way of keeping track of how the player is doing, and a nice way of unlocking villagers based on the player's actions. 

The system is simple and assigns points to different actions the player can perform, tied to different areas of the game like fishing, farming, town decoration etc. Potential villagers can now be unlocked based on these points scores, and we can also look at giving advice or tying other parts of the game to this system too if we want to.

Props
Team 17 artists have been continuing their work on items for the game. Adding more items and working through and adding textures to the existing models one by one.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/f40441dbde3e164417d824c9be7e74047a5a6a29.png

Animations
An ex-colleague, Alex from Polygon Treehouse (the lovely folks behind Röki) has been helping out with animations for the game this month. We got started working on the run and sprint animations, and now he's moved on to the emotes for the game.

https://i.imgur.com/ILaMFNV.gif
Peace emote

Icons
Jonas hopped on the project and has been helping create delightful icons for the game. Adding these to the UI really helps make the game come together, and makes things a bit more cosy too 🥰

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/88eb0b0b33f7948c6b9d331d9d28c2196852b294.png

So there you have it, all the lovely stuff we got done in October!

Next month I'll be looking at getting all the online stuff working properly, as well as making some more changes to the world map.

Hope you're all enjoying the cosy Autumn days, and keeping safe in these turbulent times.

As always, let me know your thoughts in the comments!

Speak to you soon,
from Robert

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #5
notes.content:
We’ve been incredibly busy bees these past couple of months! Robert from Wonderscope Games has the latest scoop for you… 

Dialog & Camera
I reworked the dialog system so that more than two people can have a conversation in the world! In the conversation files I added functionality that can switch between characters at different points in the dialog, as well as functions for checking if characters are nearby and triggering different conversation.

Along with this update, I worked into the camera so that it frames characters better and moves between them depending on who is talking. All this stuff will come into use in the next months when more of the intro to the game and character dialog is written.

https://i.imgur.com/GK4lCOk.gif

Town Center Unlocks
Over the course of the game you'll unlock different buildings in the town center. This month I implemented the parts required to get this working; where parts of the town center will change visually when a new building is unlocked. These buildings will be unlocked when you've become friends with their owner and they've decided to move to town.

New Character Moving-in Flow
In Hokko life, based on your actions and the type of town you build, you'll "unlock" new visitors and potential residents! Up until now when a character was unlocked, they'd start appearing in the world, wandering around a bit aimlessly at certain times of day. This felt really strange, as characters you didn't know would start showing up, and you'd often miss new animals because they'd be in an area you didn't visit for example. The initial story for this was that they'd arrive at the train station, wander around a bit and then head home; but without actually seeing their arrival, it just meant they were in the world randomly.

With the new pub/restaurant location added to the town center, visitors to your town will now appear here, either during lunch time or the evening. Once you've unlocked a new character they'll appear here and you can then talk to and befriend them. Once you've built them a house and they have moved to town they'll start wandering around and existing in the world. Setting things up this way means that you'll have a lot lower chance of missing potential residents, as they'll be at a main location at set times. It also allows for some really cozy evening chat dialog!

Once you've become good enough friends with a character, after chatting to them when they visit, you'll get the option to ask them to move in. Doing so will put them in a moving in "queue". Whenever you build a new house you can choose which character you'd like to move into that house from this list. Previously you would need to have a vacant house ready in order to ask a character to move to town, which, I felt, could cause frustration. Imagine having a character that only visits every few weeks, on a Tuesday, at lunch time, that you've finally gotten close enough with to ask them to move in, only to find you don't have a house ready! You'd have to wait until their next visit to ask them to move in, which I felt would be annoying.

Moving Boxes
When a character moves to town they'll now bring with them a bunch of items for their home and will decorate the walls and flooring in their own style. As their friend, you'll help them move in by unpacking their items and placing them where you'd like in the room. This way you get to design everyone's home, but still retain some of their personal charm (unless you hate their style, then you can just sell their stuff...! 🤫)

World Redesign
I went through the whole world of Hokko this month and redesigned it completely. 

The old world was too flat with not much variation and didn't have distinct enough areas. Alongside this, it wasn't built with progression in mind, and so the player could easily reach all areas from the beginning of the game. 

The new world comes from a paper plan I doodled, thinking about how the town would flow, allowing for different area types and how they'd all connect.

Here are some shots of the new levels:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/a5af45b0f72e3de4fc308e37e726f2613e75e0d6.png

The Bomb
Now that parts of the world are locked-off, you'll need to use both your design skills and crafting in order to progress. Several of the areas require you to design special items to access them, and others need... a bomb...!

Now there's a craftable bomb in the game (with placeholder graphics right now) which you can use to blast your way through areas blocked by rubble and rocks; for example when trying to get into the mine:

https://i.imgur.com/r0DUsCI.gif

Clothing

Here is a very small selection of some of the pieces she's created:

This month we got a new train station and builder’s hut!

So there we have it! 

With more hands on the project a lot more gets done in a month, as you can no doubt see!

I hope you're all keeping well, let me know your thoughts in the comments, or in our Discord server!

Speak soon,

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #4
notes.content:
What’s been happening with Hokko Life development? Here’s an update from Robert at Wonderscope Games!


As another month races by the summer fills the days with lovely sunsets, late night BBQs and lake swimming, and it's time for a new devlog about Hokko!

Expressions
I updated the Avatar's head shader to allow for expressions! With the new Avatar head mesh we set up the texturing so that details on the face would be handled with different textures; this means I can swap out a mouth or eye texture to provide different expressions. I edited the head shader this month to work with this and added three new emotions to the game: happy, straining, and winking.

https://i.imgur.com/3muLnuK.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/da353c7c3b26d08734381ee1cbb05d56969e570e.png

Energy
I've been contemplating for a little while adding a system similar to stamina to the game. I decided to get a first implementation of this in this month to get a feel for whether or not it made sense or felt right. I gave the player an amount of energy that they consume when performing tasks like chopping down trees or mining. Once you've depleted your energy you'll need to take a short break to recharge some of it. You'll only replenish a small amount, so you'll need to grab some food or rest if you want to do a lot more work, but it will never empty completely stopping you from working altogether. I wanted to get a nice balance, rewarding players for preparing before they go off resource gathering but not penalize them if they run out of energy.

https://i.imgur.com/3k6Lqu4.gif
Running out of energy means you'll need to catch your breath before continuing to work

We'll see if it stays or not, but it allows me to pace the activities in the game better; gives something else you can do with farmed produce; and can add some interesting gameplay to exploring the world.

As part of this energy prototype work I added jumping to the game! This will enable you to get over small gaps in the world and consumes a bit of energy. With this I'm thinking that you will unlock ways of building structures that cross these gaps as you progress later in the game, making traversal of the world smoother. One of these structures is....

Bridges! 

I added a bridge design blueprint to the game, which allows players to design their own bridges and then place them out in the world! 

https://i.imgur.com/3qZOOlv.gif
Placing a bridge I designed

Farming
Farming was one of the main focuses for this month, with the plan to expand a bit upon the simple base that was there already.

I added fertilizer to the game; it's craftable from different resources in the world and when placed on tilled soil it will increase the chances of a crop being higher quality. High quality crops can be sold for money and are sometimes requested by characters in the game. Fertilizer will be active on a patch of soil for a set amount of time and anything planted there within that duration will have it's chances tweaked.

I added templates for two new characters to the game. One is the farmer character, who will act as your introduction to farming, and will provide you with crafting recipes for your first equipment. After you've gotten under way they'll sell you different types of seeds, and some crafting recipes for things that will make your farming life easier, such as...

Sprinklers! 

I added two types of sprinkler to the game, one that waters in a ring and one that waters in a line. Once you've purchased the crafting recipe from the farmer, these can be crafted with a few resources and will make your farming life a lot easier!

https://i.imgur.com/w8VQLHi.gif

The other character I added to the game will provide you with challenges for farming, requesting numbers of produce within a certain amount of time; to enable this I expanded upon the request system to allow for deadlines.

Gardening
As part of farming I added the concept of "gardening" to the game. This essentially allows you to plant flowers and trees in the world from seeds. Previously they'd grow by themselves in various locations, but the player couldn't really move them around or plant them where they wanted. Now you can dig a hole in the ground and plant seeds that will grow over time. Trees and flowers can be planted in this way, and unlike crops they don't need watering and can be dug up and moved around as they're growing (you'll need to chop down trees when they get big though!).

This addition lets players have more control over their town and its appearance and allows you to set up areas for growing flowers for crafting too.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/59ab278bdbc8df19174de95f2712f24c6a33de33.png
Baby plants!

UI Stuff
With the new Farmer character providing you with seeds and other items for purchase I decided to build a system in the UI for displaying more detailed information on a selected item. Seeds need to show how long they take to grow, for example, and craftable items need to show what resources they require. As this was a common requirement in a lot places in the game, I built a reusable system that I can use anywhere to display this information.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/a5533f11d957b6299d2ff74db4b51eba4b94d55a.png
The styles are very WIP at the moment, but you can see the info panel on the right showing information about the seeds

Piece Packs
As you progress in the game you'll unlock more pieces you can use to design items with. This month I implemented what was needed for this to work and introduced something I'm calling "Piece Packs". Piece packs are collections of pieces you can use when designing and are unlocked as a bundle for a set price; I thought unlocking pieces in this way would be a lot more fun too! 

With Piece Packs being purchasable, I updated the Design Tool to show these packs as groups and added filter buttons allowing the player to show and hide different packs based on the materials needed.

And there we have it, all of the stuff that got done in June!

I hope you've been keeping safe and still enjoying the sunny weather.

Speak soon!
from Robert

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.content:
Here’s a fresh update on development from Robert at Wonderscope Games!

Let's get stuck into devlog #3!

FishingThe majority of this month's work has been focused on working into and expanding on the fishing gameplay. 

I thought I'd walk you through how fishing works in Hokko Life in order to show off changes made this month! 

After starting the inventory re-write last month, I was able to add bait to the game! This can be attached to a fishing rod you have equipped and will alter your chances of catching certain fish. Bait can be crafted from different resources found in the world, once you've unlocked their crafting recipes.

Right clicking on a type of bait in your backpack will give you the option of attaching it to your fishing rod:

https://i.imgur.com/f1APGdb.gif

Once your bait and hook are in the water it's a case of waiting for a fish to spot them. A fish will take a few nibbles of the bait before being hooked.

https://i.imgur.com/Itk6tmU.gif

When the fish takes the last bite and the action UI pops up, you have a short window of time to press ‘Interact’ to hook the fish. 

This will start the fishing mini game!

The aim of the fishing mini game is to keep the fish inside the ring until it reaches the goal line. The fish has a mind of its own and will try and swim away, so you'll need to position your rod left and right, and press the interact button to reel the fish back into the ring. 

If the fish is outside of the ring for too long, it'll get away and you'll fail the mini game.

https://i.imgur.com/Cm1YUD6.gif

There's also a chance a chest will appear during the mini game. If you steer the fish through this chest it'll pop open and give you a random reward!

This month I tried out a "diorama" look for the fishing mini game, building a quick little scene to make the game cuter and more appealing. It was a boring rectangle before and I like this cuter direction. Depending on where you're fishing the diorama will change in appearance too!

Fishing ChallengesI added fishing challenges to the game this month, these will unlock after you've been fishing a little while and offer a weekly challenge for players to get bonus rewards.

These challenges are generated once an in-game week and require you to catch a certain number of fish within a time limit. This can either be a specific fish, or any fish, and the time limit is adjusted based on the rarity of the fish, as well as if there are any nearby. A bunch of things happen behind the scenes too, making sure that you have a chance of winning the challenge; but don't worry, if you fail you can always go back for a retry!

I wanted to get more variation in for the challenges, but just getting them set up and working in the first place took a lot longer than expected this month, so I had to settle with just one type for now. The system's there now for future challenge types to be added in the future at least!

Avatar UpdatesI spent some more time with the avatar this month, working into the animation system, how equipping and un-equipping tools works behind the scenes among other things. The goal with these changes was primarily to make the system less buggy, as well as improve the overall appearance. Simple things like adding an acceleration to the player to make the transition from standing to running look nicer, as well as adding equip animation variations to fit the different ways the player can hold an item.

I worked into some of the animations too, improving their weighting and timing. As last month's goal was to just get animations in, it was nice to spend a few hours improving them.

https://i.imgur.com/QhkTbDH.gif

https://i.imgur.com/Vb6N22Q.gif

https://i.imgur.com/REHaLWR.gif

I also spent a little time playing with the face and head shape, getting it closer to something I'm happy with.

https://i.imgur.com/GSNGtVG.png

I added the other clothing base meshes to the game for pants, sweater and skirt and made sure they showed up in the shop for purchase. I removed all the old clothing items, as they'll need to be replaced, as well as all the old avatar assets (deleting old ugly stuff feels so good!)

I also tweaked all the old hair styles a little bit so they fit on the new head mesh. They'll need further tweaking to get them perfect, but they looked horrific before and I had to do something about it, haha!

And that, I think, is everything I worked on this month! Feels like quite a lot when I write it all out and add pictures!

Hope you're all keeping well and enjoying the start of summer as much as possible!

Speak soon!
from Robert

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #2
notes.content:
Want to know what’s been going on with Hokko Life? Robert from Wonderscope Games is here to keep you up to date with the latest dev blog!


It continues to amaze me how quickly time goes by now; that we're in May already is just crazy!
I hope you, your family, and your community are all doing alright during this time we find ourselves in.

So what got done this past month?


Publisher stuff
This month was the first proper month working with Team17. We've been having quite a few discussions and Skype calls setting things up and figuring out how we move forward. Team17 are going to be helping with some development stuff as well as publishing, so we've been getting together plans for how development will look, and I've been discussing with them my vision for the game both in terms of design and art. I put together a Game Design Document for them to outline all the features of the game and how they work, so that there's a reference there for anyone hopping onto the project.
In combination with this, I've started booking time with myself in the form of some kind of mini meetings, where I focus entirely on thinking about design, story and art for the game. It's very easy to ignore these types of things, as the allure of working directly on the game is very strong, but with a few others joining the project I decided that for everyone's benefit I needed to dedicate some time to this stuff. I've only had a few meetings so far, but they're already having a great effect on how comfortable I am with the game.

https://i.imgur.com/LVTRgbp.gif

New avatar
Content-wise I worked on getting the new avatar into the game this month. The model was created by the talented Hanna Kime (check her stuff out here: https://www.artstation.com/quickhanna) a little while back, and I had this month down for getting it in-game. I spent some time getting used to how rigging and skinning works in Blender (I was using Modo before) and then got the new avatar mesh set up ready for animation. I spent a week or so on this, followed by another week blocking out all the animations in the game. 

https://i.imgur.com/WHHoSvD.gif

The goal with the animations was to set them up to keep the game working, with the intention to work into the polish for them next month. I quickly got clothing onto the character too, and this will also be fixed up properly next month too but it felt a lot better than having a naked character running around!


https://i.imgur.com/gXbTAqZ.gif

And that's more or less it for now! Next month will focus on working into the quality of the avatar, bringing in the other base clothing meshes and improving the animations. There will be some time spent working into fishing too, making the experience a bit deeper and more refined.

Speak to you soon!

Robert

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #1
notes.content:
Check out this devblog from Robert at Wonderscope for the latest updates for Hokko Life!

Well well well, what an exciting month April was for Hokko!

We announced our partnership with Team17 and made some epic updates to Hokko Life!

Art updatesAt the start of the month I got stuck into updating the rocks in the game. Previously they’d all been colour variations of one basic rock, but now they have a distinct look depending on what type of ore they contain.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/890d1acecdfa9e8643f7008004a314dc31788bc8.png
Mine Rocks


There's now a bunch of new fish! I spent some time thinking about the style for the fish (and the rest of the game) and how I'd like them to look. I went through some iterations and decided on a clean and stylized look.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/9a77d4fb95297a7362dd79f717253379013724df.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/9b43c750c69447353251e8e49826cd12c8867a11.png
New Fish

Following on from updating the style of the fish, I wanted to tackle a building and update it to a newer style. For this I took the Workshop, one of the oldest assets in the game, and gave it a tidy-up. Cleaning up the texture and making it fit the newer style.

https://i.imgur.com/90DQ4kh.gif
Updated Workshop

I looked at the grass in the game, spending some time improving the ground texture as well as making some new 3D grass that sticks up and adds depth. I think this all makes the world feel richer and really brings the quality level up a notch.

https://i.imgur.com/KmWJ9gc.gif
New Grass

Design AnywhereNear the end of the month I started working on letting players be able to edit the design of objects in the world, just by running up to them and interacting with them. Up until now the player would need to go all the way to the workshop to edit a design and would need to have that object in their backpack to do so. Now, if you see something you'd like to edit, you can edit it from anywhere in the world. 

I'm going to continue looking at ways like this to make the game more immediate and fun, trying to remove some of the frustrating stuff that often gets in the way.

SteamI updated my process for making builds of the game and hooked it up to Steam so that I can send builds to Steam from within the Unity Editor. I'd been using Discord up until this month to send builds to my composer and others, but now it's all on Steam! Woo!

That's it for now. I hope you're all keeping well and safe.

Thanks as always for your continued support!

Robert
